base_rate_note.line1: These are estimates from a model trained on {n_total} patients who had already been referred for an angiogram, and {prev} in 100 of them had {outcome}.
base_rate_note.line2: People who haven't been referred for an angiogram usually have a much lower chance, so these numbers are not your personal risk.

display.cutoff_line: The model's cut-off for this estimate is {thr}.

dots.caption: If 100 patients had records like this one, the model expects about {p} of them to have {outcome}. Lighter dots show the range.

glossary.text: A narrowing of an artery, which can reduce blood flow.
Left anterior descending artery: runs down the front of the heart.
Left circumflex artery: wraps around the left side of the heart.
Right coronary artery: runs along the right side and underside of the heart.
An X-ray test that shows the inside of the heart's arteries. Everyone in this dataset was referred for one.
The share of blood the heart pumps out with each beat, measured by an ultrasound scan of the heart (echocardiography).
Regional wall motion abnormality: part of the heart wall moves less than it should on the ultrasound scan.
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate: a blood test that rises with inflammation.
How well the model ranks patients: 0.5 is a coin flip and 1 is perfect.
Whether estimates match reality: of patients given about 70%, roughly 70 in 100 should have the outcome.
The cut-off the model uses to call an estimate above or below. It was chosen on the training patients and is not a medical limit.
A way of writing a probability that lets contributions be added up. Positive raises the estimate, negative lowers it.
A method that splits an estimate into how much each input pushed it up or down.
How much the estimate would move if the model had learned from a slightly different set of patients. Not a guarantee.

display.headline: The model estimates a {p} probability of {outcome}{range}.

performance.accuracy: Accuracy {value}: {v100} of 100 patients were labelled correctly. Always picking the commoner group would already get {majority} of 100.
performance.brier: Brier {value}: the average squared gap between the estimate and what happened, from 0 (perfect) to 1. Lower is better; always giving the hold-out average share of {prev} would score about {ref}.
performance.f1: F1 {value}: one number that balances precision and recall; 1 is perfect.
performance.metric_example: Example for {target}, hold-out set of {n_test} patients:
performance.precision: Precision {value}: of 100 patients the model put above its cut-off, about {v100} really had {outcome}.
performance.recall: Recall {value}: the model put about {v100} of 100 patients who really had {outcome} above its cut-off.
performance.roc_auc: Shown two patients, one who has {outcome} and one who doesn't, the model gives the higher estimate to the right one about {cv} times out of 100 (cross-validated on the training patients; {holdout} out of 100 on the hold-out patients).

display.range_meaning: The range shows how much the estimate depends on which patients the model learned from. It is not a guarantee, and it is not the range of anyone's true risk.

trust.footer: All of this comes from {n_total} patients who were already referred for an angiogram, so even the fairly reliable estimates are only estimates.
trust.reliable: {id} ({label}): fairly reliable. Cross-validated ROC-AUC {auc}. The range crosses the cut-off for {n_unc} of {n} hold-out patients.
trust.rule: “Fairly reliable” means a cross-validated ROC-AUC of at least {min_auc}. This is a rule of thumb, not a clinical standard.
trust.title: How much to trust each estimate
trust.weak: {id} ({label}): weak. Cross-validated ROC-AUC {auc}. The range crosses the cut-off for {n_unc} of {n} hold-out patients, so this estimate is much less certain.

waterfall.baseline_caption: Where the model starts for an average patient in its training data. This is the model's baseline for {target} ({base}), not the {prev} of dataset patients who had {outcome}; the two can differ.
waterfall.order_caption: Each step adds to the one before it and is shown in percentage points. Step sizes depend on the order of the steps, so read them as a rough guide, not exact amounts.
waterfall.technical_line: Log-odds contributions (SHAP) behind the steps above. Baseline log-odds {base_logit}; the contributions add up exactly to the calibrated log-odds {logit}, which is {p}.
waterfall.title: How the model got to {p}

features.help: Age in whole years at the time of the tests.
features.label: Age

features.help: Sex as recorded in the patient's file (male or female).
features.label: Sex

features.help: Body weight in kilograms. Used with height to work out BMI.
features.label: Weight

features.help: Height in centimetres. Used with weight to work out BMI.
features.label: Height

features.help: Body mass index, calculated as weight divided by height squared. You don't enter it.
features.label: BMI

features.help: Marked "yes" when BMI is above 25, which is how the training data defines it (most guidelines use 30). You don't enter it.
features.label: Obesity

features.help: Diabetes mellitus: long-term high blood sugar. Usually in the medical history or medication list.
features.label: Diabetes mellitus

features.help: Hypertension: long-term high blood pressure. Usually in the medical history or medication list.
features.label: Hypertension

features.help: Never, currently smoking, or stopped (former). Asked at an intake or history interview.
features.label: Smoking status

features.help: A close relative with coronary artery disease, as recorded in the patient's history. Asked at an intake interview.
features.label: Family history of CAD

features.help: Dyslipidemia: abnormal blood fats such as high LDL or triglycerides. In the history or on a lipid profile.
features.label: Dyslipidemia

features.help: Chronic renal failure: long-term reduced kidney function. In the medical history.
features.label: Chronic renal failure

features.help: A previous stroke (cerebrovascular accident). In the medical history.
features.label: Prior stroke (CVA)

features.help: Long-term lung or airway disease such as asthma or COPD. In the medical history.
features.label: Airway disease

features.help: A known thyroid condition, over- or under-active. In the medical history.
features.label: Thyroid disease

features.help: Congestive heart failure: the heart doesn't pump as well as the body needs. In the medical history.
features.label: Congestive heart failure

features.help: Systolic ("top number") blood pressure at rest, in mmHg. From a blood pressure reading.
features.label: Systolic blood pressure

features.help: Pulse rate: heartbeats per minute at rest. From a pulse check or the vital signs.
features.label: Pulse rate

features.help: The type of chest pain, if any. Typical angina: pressure or tightness brought on by effort and eased by rest. Atypical: some but not all of those features. Non-anginal: chest pain without the usual features of angina. From the symptom history.
features.label: Chest pain type

features.help: Chest pain that comes on with only light effort. From the symptom history.
features.label: Low-threshold angina

features.help: Shortness of breath. From the symptom history.
features.label: Dyspnea

features.help: How much everyday activity is limited by symptoms, from 0, not limited, to 3, most limited. A clinician's rating.
features.label: Functional class

features.help: Swelling from fluid, usually in the ankles or legs. Found on examination.
features.label: Edema

features.help: A faint pulse in the arms or legs. Found on examination.
features.label: Weak peripheral pulse

features.help: Crackling sounds in the lungs heard through a stethoscope. Found on examination.
features.label: Lung rales

features.help: An extra "whoosh" sound between the main heart sounds. Heard with a stethoscope.
features.label: Systolic murmur

features.help: An extra "whoosh" sound after the second heart sound. Heard with a stethoscope.
features.label: Diastolic murmur

features.help: A pathological Q wave: a deep early dip that can mark an old area of damaged heart muscle. On the ECG report.
features.label: Q wave

features.help: The ST segment sits above the baseline. On the ECG report.
features.label: ST elevation

features.help: The ST segment sits below the baseline. On the ECG report.
features.label: ST depression

features.help: The T wave points downward instead of upward. On the ECG report.
features.label: T inversion

features.help: Left ventricular hypertrophy: a thickened left pumping chamber, reported from the ECG. On the ECG report.
features.label: LV hypertrophy

features.help: The R waves don't grow across the chest leads as expected. On the ECG report.
features.label: Poor R-wave progression

features.help: Bundle branch block: a delay in the heart's electrical wiring, left or right. On the ECG report.
features.label: Bundle branch block

features.help: Fasting blood sugar (glucose), measured after fasting, usually overnight. On a blood glucose or metabolic panel.
features.label: Fasting blood sugar

features.help: Creatinine: a waste product cleared by the kidneys. On a kidney or metabolic panel.
features.label: Creatinine

features.help: Triglycerides: a type of blood fat. On a lipid profile.
features.label: Triglycerides

features.help: LDL cholesterol, often called "bad" cholesterol. On a lipid profile.
features.label: LDL cholesterol

features.help: HDL cholesterol, often called "good" cholesterol. On a lipid profile.
features.label: HDL cholesterol

features.help: Blood urea nitrogen: another waste product cleared by the kidneys. On a kidney or metabolic panel.
features.label: Blood urea nitrogen

features.help: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate: how fast red cells settle in a tube, a general marker of inflammation. On a blood test report.
features.label: ESR

features.help: Hemoglobin: the oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells. On a complete blood count (CBC).
features.label: Hemoglobin

features.help: Potassium, a blood salt. On a metabolic panel.
features.label: Potassium

features.help: Sodium, a blood salt. On a metabolic panel.
features.label: Sodium

features.help: White blood cell count. On a complete blood count (CBC).
features.label: White blood cells

features.help: Lymphocytes, a type of white cell, as a percent of all white cells. On the CBC differential.
features.label: Lymphocytes

features.help: Neutrophils, a type of white cell, as a percent of all white cells. On the CBC differential.
features.label: Neutrophils

features.help: Platelet count: the cells that help blood clot. On a complete blood count (CBC).
features.label: Platelets

features.help: Ejection fraction: the share of blood the left chamber pumps out with each beat, from a transthoracic echo (TTE). On the echo report.
features.label: Ejection fraction (TTE)

features.help: How many of the heart wall's regions (0–4) move abnormally. On the echo report ("regional wall-motion abnormality").
features.label: Regions with wall-motion abnormality

features.help: Valvular heart disease: a leaking or narrowed heart valve, graded none to severe. On the echo report.
features.label: Valvular heart disease
